newsitem.title: USA: Montana seeding nearly complete, rains help crops.
newsitem.headline: Montana seeding nearly complete, rains help crops.

text.p: Rains in the week ended Sunday helped crops and pastures throughout Montana, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly update.
There were 4.1 days suitable for fieldwork. Sugar beet planting, including reseedings due to freezing, was complete and corn, wheat and barley all 95 percent seeded or more.
"Planting and emergence of small grains and most row crops is above last year and average," it said.
Spring wheat seeded 96 percent vs 91 week ago, 94 year ago and 97 on a 5-year average.
Spring wheat emerged 84 pct vs 60 w/a, 74 y/a, 83 avge.
Spring wheat rated 65 percent good to excellent versus 51 last week, 32 pct fair vs 42 last week.
Barley planted 98 pct vs 92 week ago, 93 year ago, 95 avg.
Barley emerged 83 pct vs 55 w/a, 71 y/a, 78 avg.
Barley rated 72 percent good to excellent versus 55 last week, 26 pct fair vs 42 last week.
Winter wheat rated 57 percent good to excellent versus 50 last week, 29 pct fair vs 33 last week, and 14 pct poor or very poor vs 17 last week.
Corn planted 95 pct vs 93 week ago, 90 year ago, 93 avg.
Corn emerged 86 pct vs 50 w/a, 57 y/a, avg unavailable.
Oats planted 95 pct vs 81 w/a, 85 y/a, 93 avg.
Oats emerged 77 pct vs 52 w/a, 62 y/a, 73 avg.
Oats rated 53 percent good to excellent versus 49 last week, 44 pct fair vs 42 last week.
Sugarbeets planted 100 pct vs 100 w/a, 100 y/a, 100 avg.
Sugarbeets emerged 97 pct vs 89 w/a, 97 y/a, avg unavail.

Pasture and range was rated 54 percent good to excellent, versus 38 percent a week earlier. Topsoil moisture was rated 5 percent very short, 11 pct short, 78 pct adequate, 6 pct surplus, all up sharply on last week; subsoils were rated 5 pct very short, 26 pct short, 63 pct adequate, 6 pct surplus, up slightly on last week.
